_comment: Reference only. Intercom's Developer Hub has no manifest-file or CLI mechanism (confirmed by web search — unlike Zendesk's zcli + manifest.json, apps are registered and configured entirely through the Developer Hub web UI). This file documents the exact values a human enters into that UI so they don't have to be reconstructed from memory; Intercom never reads this file.

app.name: Anakin
app.description: Scrape, crawl, or map URLs; run AI search or agentic research; look up live data on hundreds of sites with Wire; and check website monitors — all from the conversation sidebar.
app.workspace: <the Intercom workspace this app is created in — Developer Hub > Your apps > New app>

authentication._comment: Configure > Authentication. Client Secret is generated by Intercom when the app is created; copy it into this server's INTERCOM_CLIENT_SECRET env var.
authentication.client_secret: <generated by Intercom on app creation — set as INTERCOM_CLIENT_SECRET on this server, never commit it>

canvas_kit._comment: Configure > Canvas Kit > For teammates. 'Add to conversation details' places the app in the Inbox conversation sidebar, matching this server's design (support agent working an open conversation).

permissions._comment: This app makes no calls back into the Intercom REST API (it only calls api.anakin.io server-side), so no Intercom API scopes are required beyond the default Canvas Kit webhook access every Inbox app gets.

environment._comment: Server-side env vars this deployment needs (see .env.example).
environment.ANAKIN_API_KEY: <from https://anakin.io/dashboard — 300 free credits, no card required>
